issues.description: Close message type is 'Close' but the PR description and Deepgram docs say 'CloseStream'
issues.detail: The constant sends {"type": "Close"} but the entire PR title, description, and the referenced Deepgram control message spec say CloseStream. If the spec is right, this patch does not actually do what it claims and the server will ignore an unknown message type. Verify against the live API and fix the string, or fix the description. One of them is wrong.

issues.description: Flush was silently added; PR claims to only send CloseStream
issues.detail: The diff sends Flush then Close, but the commit message and PR description only mention CloseStream. That is two changes in one patch with one of them undocumented. Either Flush is needed (then say so and justify it) or it isn't (then drop it). Maintainer six months from now reading the bisect will curse you.

issues.description: Bare except Exception swallows everything including CancelledError concerns
issues.detail: except Exception as e with a warning log hides real bugs. ConnectionResetError during shutdown is expected and shouldn't warn; a programming error should not be downgraded to a log line. Catch the specific aiohttp/connection errors you actually expect, or don't catch at all. The logger.warning will create noise on every normal disconnect.

issues.description: Single receive() with 1s timeout does not guarantee 'final messages' are drained
issues.detail: Comment says 'wait for final messages' (plural) but code does exactly one receive() then moves on. If Deepgram sends audio frames before the close ack, you drop them and close mid-stream — the exact bug the patch claims to fix. Either loop draining until you see the close ack/CLOSED frame, or rewrite the comment to match what the code does.

issues.description: No test demonstrating the bug or the fix
issues.detail: Claim: audio was being truncated. Evidence: none in the diff. A failing test that captures the truncation, then passes after the patch, is how you prove this works and how you prevent regression. Prose in the commit message is not a regression suite. The STT side allegedly does this correctly — mirror its test if one exists.

issues.description: Constants defined as class attributes via json.dumps run at import time but are private to one method
issues.detail: _FLUSH_MSG and _CLOSE_MSG are class-level only because _close_ws happens to be on the instance class — but _close_ws is on the parent TTS class, not SynthesizeStream. The reference SynthesizeStream._FLUSH_MSG from _close_ws couples two classes oddly. Either move the constants to where they're used, or make this coupling explicit.

review.summary: The patch tries to do the right thing — graceful close before WebSocket termination — but the diff and the description don't match. The PR says CloseStream, the code sends Close; the PR mentions one message, the code sends two. That alone is grounds to bounce it back. Beyond the message-name discrepancy, the drain logic is a single receive() that won't actually wait for "final messages" as the comment claims, and the broad except Exception will paper over real failures with warning logs on every normal disconnect. No test, no proof the original bug existed or is fixed. NEEDS-WORK: reconcile the message name with Deepgram's spec, justify or drop Flush, loop the drain until the close frame, narrow the exception, add a test.
